newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks close at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks close at record high.

text.p: Swiss shares set a new record closing high after an early boost in the financial sector and a late dollar rally pushed prices ahead.
Dealers said investor interest was focused on financials, cyclicals and consumer stocks.
The SMI index of leading shares rose 30.7 points, or 0.8 percent, to 3,856.4, after reaching a record intraday high of 3,859.3. The broad SPI index finished 19.66 points higher at 2,463.63.
CS Holding registered shares jumped 3.75 francs to 132.50 while UBS bearers and SBC rose about one-half percent.
Winterthur Insurance rose 13 francs to 777. Dealers said there was speculation that the company might sell its stake in France's UAP.
Winterthur-Europe in Belgium will hold a news conference on Monday to talk about an insurance alliance.
Zurich Insurance jumped seven francs to 364.
Roche rose 110 francs to 9,845 francs while Ciba and Sandoz were nearly unchanged.
Most cyclical stocks also were higher.
Swissair fell 15 francs to 1,004 after a downgrading to "hold" from "buy" by UBS Research, dealers said.

Trading on the futures and options exchange Soffex was more active, profiting from strong gains in some stocks in the underlying market and the break through resistance at 3,835/40 points in the SMI, dealers said.
Options volume on the Soffex totalled 139,064 contracts. SMI futures turnover was 14,666 contracts.
